name: Motorized Bicycle
description: A two-wheeled vehicle that can be propelled by human power, a helper motor, or both, with a motor rated at no more than 4.9 horsepower and a top speed of 30 mph; the DMV registers it as a moped. An electric bike whose motor tops an electric motorized bicycle's 2 horsepower, or that goes faster than 28 mph, lands here while it stays within these limits. Defined by Rhode Island General Laws §31-1-3(p) and regulated by chapter 31-19.1.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels, propelled by human power, its motor, or both
Its motor is rated at no more than 4.9 horsepower (about 3,675 W); the statute's 50 cc cap is a combustion-engine measure
Riders need a valid driver's license and must be 16 or older; no motorcycle license needed
Registered with the DMV as a moped and carries a registration plate
One faster than 30 mph or with a motor over 4.9 horsepower is a motor-driven cycle or a motorcycle, which needs a motorcycle license
